newsitem.title: USA: N.Carolina judge limits ABC-TV financial exposure.
newsitem.headline: N.Carolina judge limits ABC-TV financial exposure.

text.p: A federal judge ruled that Food Lion could not seek an estimated $1.7 billion in damages from Walt Disney Co's ABC Television after a jury found network journalists liable for fraud in an expose of the grocery store chain.

U.S. District Judge N.Carlton Tilley, in a ruling moments after a jury verdict was announced, said Food Lion could not seek damages for lost sales or diminished stock value from the November 5, 1992 broadcast of the "PrimeTime Live" report.

The judge said Food Lion will be limited to seeking damages in the form of wages paid to the undercover ABC employees, the cost of hiring replacement employees, plus punitive damages. A lawyer for Food Lion told reporters outside the courtroom the grocery store chain would review the ruling before deciding whether or not to appeal.

Food Lion, the U.S. unit of Belgian retailer Ets Delhaize Freres et Cie "LE LION' SA, claims it lost $1.5 billion in stock value at the time of the Nov. 5, 1992 broadcast, and $233 million in profits after the broadcast.
The jury found four ABC producers liable for various fraud charges in gathering undercover video pictures of Food Lion employees improperly handling fresh meat and chicken.
